**Synopsis:**
The US has expanded secondary sanctions targeting Iran's oil revenues, focusing pressure on Chinese buyers — particularly independent "teapot" refineries — who are the primary offtakers of discounted Iranian crude. Chinese imports of Iranian oil have fallen sharply from ~1.57 mb/d in February to ~534k b/d in August 2025, largely due to a US naval blockade of Iranian ports reimposed in July. Washington is deliberately avoiding sanctioning large Chinese banks ahead of anticipated Trump-Xi talks, wary of Chinese retaliation including restrictions on critical mineral exports. Beijing has officially rejected the sanctions and vowed to protect its interests. The situation remains fluid and diplomatically charged.
